messages.content:
The method ClassUtils.toClass(Object[]) aims to convert an array of Objects to an array of Classes representing the runtime classes of those objects. 

- The test `testToClass_object()` calls ClassUtils.toClass with an array containing { "Test", null, 99d } (String, null, Double).
- The issue report states that c0.m0(Object[]) (most likely ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])) throws a NullPointerException (NPE) on a null element in the input array.
- Examining the method implementation:
  - If the input array is null, it returns null.
  - If the array is empty, it returns an empty Class array.
  - Otherwise, it creates a Class<?>[] of the same length.
  - It then iterates over the input array and does classes[i] = array[i].getClass().
- This last line is problematic if array[i] is null. Calling getClass() on a null element will cause a NullPointerException.
- Since the test input array contains a null at index 1, the method will throw an NPE when trying to call getClass() on that null.
- The test clearly expects that the output array contains null at the corresponding index (so the expected output was String.class, null, Double.class).
- Thus, the bug is that the implementation does not check for null elements in the input array before calling getClass().

Recent bug reports do not seem directly relevant nor do they mention similar null pointer issues.

Diagnosis:
The bug is caused by the code at line 910 in ClassUtils.toClass(Object[]) where it calls array[i].getClass() without null checking. If array[i] is null, this throws an NPE instead of inserting null in the output Class[] array. The test fails with a NullPointerException because the test input contains null elements. The method should be modified to check if array[i] is null and assign null to classes[i] in that case, to correctly handle null elements.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
